210	title: "Canvas background and timecode"
211	description: "Set the colour behind every layer, make the canvas transparent, choose how times are shown, and decide how new clips are sized."
212	---
213	
214	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
215	
216	The **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) sets three things for the whole project: the colour behind your clips, how times are written, and how big a new clip starts.
217	
218	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Appearance" tools={['set_canvas', 'add_clip']} />
219	
220	| Control | What it does | Default |
221	| --- | --- | --- |
222	| **Background** | The colour behind every layer. | Black, opaque |
223	| **Timecode** | How the project shows a time. | Frames |
224	| **Fit new clips to canvas** | Scales down a new clip that's bigger than the canvas. | On |
225	
226	A change to **Timecode** or **Fit new clips to canvas** is one undo step.
227	
228	## Set the background colour
229	
230	Click the **Background** swatch and pick a colour in the Colors panel. The colour sits behind every layer, so it shows wherever no clip covers the canvas.
231	
232	To put a colour on the timeline as a clip instead, see [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
233	
234	## Make the background transparent
235	
236	Lower the opacity in the Colors panel. The swatch shows a checkerboard behind the colour, and the **Background** row of the [Document summary](/projects/document-tab/#the-document-summary) reads `Transparent`, or the colour with its opacity.
237	
238	Most export formats can't carry transparency, so while the background isn't fully opaque, the section adds a note about the formats that can.
239	
240	| The note says | When |
241	| --- | --- |
242	| "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats." | Three or more formats keep it, so the note counts them. They're HEVC with Alpha (MOV), VP9 with Alpha (WebM), ProRes 4444 (MOV) and Animated PNG. |
243	| "Transparent — needs an alpha format." | Frame Job can't name the formats yet, which can happen on a project with nothing on the timeline. |
244	
245	See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).
246	
247	## Choose a timecode format
248	
249	**Timecode** sets how times are written everywhere the project shows one, including the toolbar, the ruler, the inspector, markers and the transcript.
250	
251	| Choice | Looks like |
252	| --- | --- |
253	| **Frames** | `HH:MM:SS:FF` |
254	| **Milliseconds** | `HH:MM:SS.mmm` |
255	
256	**Frames** doesn't drop frames, so at 29.97 fps the count runs slightly behind the clock over a long timeline.
257	
258	## Fit new clips to canvas
259	
260	This decides how big a new clip starts. It's on by default.
261	
262	| Setting | A clip bigger than the canvas | Any other clip |
263	| --- | --- | --- |
264	| On | Starts at Fit scale: scaled down until all of it shows. | Starts at 100 %, its native size. |
265	| Off | Starts at 100 %, so it runs past the edges of the canvas. | Starts at 100 %. |
266	
267	A clip counts as bigger when either its width or its height is larger than the canvas. Fit never scales a clip up, and changing the setting leaves clips already on the timeline as they are. To fit or fill one clip, see [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/).
268	
269	## Reset the section
270	
271	**Reset** on the **Appearance** header puts all three back to their defaults: opaque black, **Frames** and on. It's offered only while one of them differs, and it's one undo step.
272	
273	## With an agent
274	
275	`set_canvas` sets all three, and anything it doesn't name keeps its value.
276	
277	| Argument | What it takes |
278	| --- | --- |
279	| `background` | Four numbers from 0 to 1, `[r, g, b, a]`. Three numbers, or one outside the range, fails and nothing changes. |
280	| `timecode_frames` | `true` for **Frames**, `false` for **Milliseconds**. |
281	| `fit_new_clips` | `true` or `false`, as the checkbox. |
282	
283	`add_clip` follows **Fit new clips to canvas** as the app does. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
284

293	title: "Import media"
294	description: "Bring movies, sound, pictures and LUTs into a project with Add Media… or a Finder drop, and find out why a file won't come in."
295	---
296	
297	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
298	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
299	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
300	
301	Importing puts a file in the project's Media tab, ready to place on the timeline. Frame Job reads the file from where it already is, so nothing is copied and the project stays small.
302	
303	<AtAGlance
304	  menu="File ▸ Add Media…"
305	  keys="⇧⌘I"
306	  where={['Media tab ▸ Add Media…', 'Drag from the Finder onto the Media tab']}
307	  tools={['import_media', 'add_media']}
308	/>
309	
310	<Shot
311	  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
312	  alt="The Media tab of the inspector, with the Add Media… button and its ⇧⌘I shortcut at the top of the list, and a count of the project's items beside them."
313	/>
314	
315	## Add media
316	
317	<Steps>
318	
319	1. Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>), or **Add Media…** at the top of the Media tab.
320	
321	2. Pick one or more files, and choose **Open**.
322	
323	</Steps>
324	
325	Frame Job checks every file, then adds the ones it can read to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) together, as one undo step. The step is called **Add Media**, or **Add 3 Media Files** for three.
326	
327	The files are in the Media tab, not on the timeline. [Place them](/editing/add-clips/) from there. Thumbnails and waveforms are built in the background, so they fill in a moment later.
328	
329	Adding a file that's already in the list changes nothing. A file Frame Job can't read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added.
330	
331	## Drop on the Media tab
332	
333	Drag files from the Finder onto the Media tab to add them to this project. It works like **Add Media…**, with one difference: a drop has no list of allowed types, so Frame Job tries every file you drop. That's how a format the panels don't list gets in.
334	
335	A Finder drop anywhere else on the window, such as the canvas or the timeline, doesn't add to this project. It opens the file as a new project of its own, as a drop on the Dock icon does. See [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
336	
337	## What each way takes
338	
339	The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels only let you pick the types they list. To bring in anything else, drop it on the Media tab.
340	
341	| Files | **Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…**, or a drop on the window or the Dock | A drop on the Media tab |
342	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
343	| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
344	| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
345	| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
346	| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
347	| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
348	| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |
349	
350	A `.cube` is imported, never opened. It sits in the Media tab and you apply it to clips as a [look](/color/luts/), or to a file as its [camera log](/hdr/log-luts/). It never goes on the timeline.
351	
352	Caption files aren't media. Bring an `.srt` in with [Import Captions](/captions/import-captions/). Every format and codec Frame Job reads is listed in [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
353	
354	## Referenced, not copied
355	
356	A project remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark, and reads the file from there. The package stays small, but it depends on your footage staying put. If you move a file, the bookmark often finds it again.
357	
358	When you want a package that holds everything it needs, use [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).
359	
360	WebM and Matroska files, and anything converted with ffmpeg, are the exception: Frame Job reads those from a copy it keeps in its own folder. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
361	
362	## A project always opens
363	
364	A project opens even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, and their rows in the Media tab wear the **missing** badge.
365	
366	Those clips still export, showing the slate and with no sound. To bring them back, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
367	
368	## Codecs this Mac can't decode
369	
370	Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame. If nothing on this Mac can decode it, the file is left out and an alert names the codec.
371	
372	| The alert says | What it means |
373	| --- | --- |
374	| "*file* is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode." | VP8 doesn't import. |
375	| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | AV1 needs a hardware decoder, which this Mac doesn't have. |
376	| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | VP9 Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. Profiles 0 and 2 do. |
377	
378	Any other codec gets the same sentence with its four-character code in place of a name. There's no way past these, and [ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) isn't offered.
379	
380	A file in a codec this Mac does decode still imports when some of its data is damaged.
381	
382	## Import errors
383	
384	| The alert says | What it means |
385	| --- | --- |
386	| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
387	| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
388	| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took more than 30 seconds, usually because the file is on a stalled network volume. |
389	| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The `.cube` can't be read. The alert names the line and the problem. |
390	
391	If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job may offer to convert a file before it shows the first two of these. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
392	
393	## Good to know
394	
395	- A project holds at most 1,024 media files.
396	- Undoing an import takes the files out of the project and leaves them on disk.
397	
398	## With an agent
399	
400	`import_media` does what **Add Media…** does, one file at a time, and it never stops to ask a question. It takes the file's path, absolute or starting with `~`, and gives back the new media id with what it found in the file: its kind, length, size, frame rate, and whether it has video, sound or transparency. Place the file with `add_clip`.
401	
402	`add_media` is different: it adds an entry from a description you supply and doesn't look at the file. Only the path is needed, and a path already in the list changes nothing. Use it only to replay a project's own JSON. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
403

412	title: "WebM and Matroska files"
413	description: "How Frame Job brings in .webm and .mkv files by copying their streams into a movie, what the copy can carry, and where the copies live."
414	---
415	
416	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
417	
418	macOS won't open a WebM or MKV file directly, so Frame Job copies its video and sound into a QuickTime movie the first time you bring one in. Nothing is re-encoded, so no quality is lost, and your original stays where it is.
419	
420	<AtAGlance
421	  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…']}
422	  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
423	  where="Drag to the Media tab"
424	  tools={['import_media', 'open_project', 'relink_media']}
425	/>
426	
427	## How a file is rewrapped
428	
429	Rewrapping means moving a file's video and sound streams into a different container without changing them. Add, open or relink the file as you would any other. There's no question to answer: the copy starts by itself, and the clip then plays from the copy.
430	
431	Frame Job recognises these files by what's inside them, not by their name, so a Matroska file with the wrong extension still imports when you drop it on the Media tab, unless that extension is a picture's or `.cube`.
432	
433	| Stream | What the copy carries |
434	| --- | --- |
435	| Video | VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC |
436	| Sound | Opus, Vorbis or AAC |
437	
438	Only the first video track and the first audio track are copied. Any other track, such as a second language or subtitles, stays behind in the original.
439	
440	If the end of the file is damaged or cut short, the copy holds everything up to that point.
441	
442	Some video can't come in because this Mac can't decode it: VP8, AV1 on a Mac without a hardware decoder, and VP9 Profile 1 or 3. Nothing is copied, and the alert says why. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
443	
444	## The name in the Media tab
445	
446	The media keeps the original's name. Hover over its row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) and the tooltip gives the original's path and says the file was copied into Frame Job's Rewrapped folder.
447	
448	## The Copying Movie window
449	
450	A copy that takes more than a second shows a small **Copying Movie** window, with a progress bar and how much has been copied, such as "412 MB of 1.2 GB". It reads "Reading the file…" until the copy starts.
451	
452	Choose **Cancel** to stop. The copy stops, nothing is added, no alert appears and no partial file is left behind. If you were opening the file with **File ▸ Open…**, no project opens. If you were adding several files, the others carry on.
453	
454	The window never takes the keyboard from a Frame Job window, so you can keep editing while it runs. Copies happen one at a time.
455	
456	## Free space
457	
458	Before copying, Frame Job checks that the disk has room. If it doesn't, nothing is copied and the alert says what's needed:
459	
460	> Not enough free space to open *file*: its video and sound need about *size* on “*volume*”, which has *size* free. Nothing was copied.
461	
462	If Frame Job can't read how much space the volume has, the copy goes ahead.
463	
464	## The Rewrapped folder
465	
466	Copies live in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, which all your projects share. Importing the same file again uses its copy instead of making another, even in a different project. If the original has changed, Frame Job makes a new copy.
467	
468	Frame Job doesn't clear this folder, so copies pile up. You can clear it yourself:
469	
470	- WebM and MKV copies are made again the next time a project that uses them opens, as long as the original is still there.
471	- [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#a-lost-conversion-stays-missing) live here too, and they aren't made again. Their media stays missing until you relink it.
472	
473	[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies the movie, not the WebM, into the package. The row's tooltip then says it was copied into this project's package.
474	
475	## Streams the copy can't carry
476	
477	If a stream is in a codec the copy can't carry, the file isn't added, and an alert names the stream, for example:
478	
479	> *file* has FLAC audio, which Frame Job cannot copy out of a WebM or Matroska file.
480	
481	This applies to FLAC, MP3, MP2, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, TrueHD and PCM sound, Vorbis whose headers can't be read, and MPEG-2, MPEG-4 Part 2, Theora and ProRes video. A codec without a familiar name appears under its Matroska codec ID. A compressed or encrypted track stops the import the same way: "*file* has a compressed or encrypted video track, which Frame Job cannot copy out of a WebM or Matroska file."
482	
483	If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job then offers to help. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Without it, the file isn't added.
484	
485	## Colour is kept
486	
487	The copy keeps the colour the file states: HLG, HDR10 (PQ), or a BT.709, BT.601 or BT.2020 SDR picture. Frame Job reads it from the file's colour information or, for VP9, from the video itself. HDR10 metadata carries over.
488	
489	A file that states no colour is shown as macOS reads it.
490	
491	## If a copy goes missing
492	
493	If a copy is deleted or moved to the Trash, the project makes it again from the original the next time it opens. The **Copying Movie** window shows as usual.
494	
495	This needs the original to be in place and still be a WebM or Matroska file. If that copy is cancelled or fails, a deleted copy shows as missing, with a slate, the **missing** badge and **Relink…**, and a copy in the Trash goes on playing from the Trash. The next open tries again.
496	
497	## With an agent
498	
499	An agent's import shows no window and waits for the copy to finish. `import_media` gives the copy as `path` and the file you asked for as `original`. If the copy can't carry a stream, an agent doesn't get the ffmpeg question: see [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#with-an-agent).
500

504	- [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/)

506	- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)

509	title: "Convert files with ffmpeg"
510	description: "Use your own ffmpeg to bring in a file macOS can't open: what Frame Job asks, what it copies or re-encodes, and how to change your answer."
511	---
512	
513	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
514	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
515	
516	When macOS can't open a file and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can use it to repackage or convert the file on import. Frame Job doesn't include ffmpeg, and without your own copy this step never appears.
517	
518	<AtAGlance
519	  where={['The alert that appears on import ▸ Repackage or Convert']}
520	  tools={['import_media', 'relink_media']}
521	  needs="Your own ffmpeg and ffprobe, both installed on this Mac."
522	/>
523	
524	## Repackage or convert a file
525	
526	<Steps>
527	
528	1. Add, open or relink the file as usual. If macOS can't open it, an alert appears: "Frame Job cannot open “*file*”."
529	
530	2. Read what it would cost. The alert names the codecs and gives the size and the time.
531	
532	3. Choose **Repackage** or **Convert** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to leave the file out.
533	
534	</Steps>
535	
536	The first button reads **Repackage** or **Convert** depending on the work to be done:
537	
538	| The button | What the alert tells you |
539	| --- | --- |
540	| **Repackage** | Every stream can be copied as it is. No re-encoding, no loss of quality, and a few seconds' work. |
541	| **Convert** | The video can be copied, but the sound has to be re-encoded to AAC. That also takes a few seconds. |
542	| **Convert** | This Mac can't decode the video, so the whole file has to be re-encoded to H.264. The alert gives its picture size and length, and says it takes at least as long as the clip runs, usually longer. |
543	
544	If you choose **Cancel**, Frame Job then shows the reason it couldn't read the file.
545	
546	A conversion shows no progress window. The file appears when it's finished. If you add several files that need this step, Frame Job asks about them one at a time.
547	
548	## What's copied and what's re-encoded
549	
550	Each stream is copied when it can be, and re-encoded when it can't.
551	
552	| Stream | Copied unchanged | Otherwise |
553	| --- | --- | --- |
554	| Video | H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4, QuickTime Animation and DV | Re-encoded to H.264 |
555	| Sound | AAC, ALAC and the usual 16-, 24- and 32-bit PCM | Re-encoded to 256 kbps AAC |
556	
557	The H.264 encode uses x264 at CRF 18 when your ffmpeg has it. Without x264 it uses Apple's VideoToolbox encoder, at a bitrate worked out from the picture size and frame rate, from 2 to 60 Mbps. Either way the result is 8-bit 4:2:0, so a 10-bit source comes in as 8-bit.
558	
559	VP9 Profile 0 or 2 with a known frame rate is copied too, with AAC or ALAC sound beside it, and any other sound is re-encoded to AAC. Frame Job then checks that every frame of the copy sits exactly on the frame rate. If the copy fails that check, or won't open, it's re-encoded to H.264 once. Unless you've told Frame Job to do this automatically, it asks you again first.
560	
561	Only the first video stream and the first audio stream are carried over. Subtitles and data streams are dropped.
562	
563	## Where the converted file goes
564	
565	The converted file goes into `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, the same folder as [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#the-rewrapped-folder). It keeps its own name in the Media tab, and your original is untouched.
566	
567	Importing the same file again uses the finished conversion with no question, even if you've since removed ffmpeg or chosen never to convert. If the original's path, size or modification date has changed, it counts as a new file.
568	
569	## Remember your answer
570	
571	Tick **Do this automatically from now on** in the alert to keep the answer you give:
572	
573	- Ticked with **Repackage** or **Convert**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
574	- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails with its usual message.
575	
576	There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:
577	
578	```sh
579	defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
580	```
581	
582	That setting holds `ask`, `always` or `never`, and `ask` is the default.
583	
584	## Finding ffmpeg
585	
586	Frame Job needs both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. With only one of them, this step doesn't appear.
587	
588	It looks on your `PATH` first, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`. It looks once per launch, so quit and reopen Frame Job after installing ffmpeg.
589	
590	To use one particular build, name it in Terminal:
591	
592	```sh
593	defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg
594	```
595	
596	`ffprobe` is then taken from beside it, or else found by the same search. If nothing runnable is at that path, Frame Job doesn't look anywhere else for `ffmpeg`, and this step doesn't appear.
597	
598	## When a conversion fails
599	
600	| The alert says | What it means |
601	| --- | --- |
602	| "Could not convert *file* with ffmpeg: *reason*" | ffmpeg stopped with an error. The reason is its own last line, and without one the sentence ends at "ffmpeg." |
603	| "ffmpeg gave up converting *file*." | It ran out of time. |
604	
605	A **Repackage** gets five minutes or twice the file's length, whichever is longer. A **Convert** gets 30 minutes or 30 times the file's length, whichever is longer. Neither gets more than 4 hours.
606	
607	No partial file is left behind. If a conversion finishes but macOS still can't open the result, Frame Job throws it away and shows the original error, so the next import starts afresh.
608	
609	## A lost conversion stays missing
610	
611	Unlike a [WebM copy](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#if-a-copy-goes-missing), a conversion that's deleted isn't made again when the project opens. The media stays missing until you [relink it](/projects/relink-media/). Relinking to the original file goes through this step again.
612	
613	A conversion you've only moved is treated like any other file: its [bookmark](/projects/import-media/#referenced-not-copied) often finds it again. One moved to the Trash goes on playing from the Trash.
614	
615	## Files ffmpeg isn't offered for
616	
617	Frame Job doesn't offer ffmpeg for:
618	
619	- A picture or a `.cube` file it can't read.
620	- A file that timed out, because ffmpeg would stall on the same volume.
621	- A codec this Mac can't decode inside a file macOS can open, or inside a WebM or MKV file. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
622	- A WebM or MKV file stopped by the [free-space check](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#free-space).
623	- A file in which ffprobe finds no video or audio.
624	
625	## With an agent
626	
627	An agent's import never shows this question. Unless you've chosen to convert automatically, the offer counts as declined, and the import fails and gives the reason. While the answer is still `ask` and ffmpeg is installed, the error also says how to get past it: import the file from the app's window, or set the answer to `always`.
628	
629	To set it, tick [**Do this automatically from now on**](#remember-your-answer) with **Repackage** or **Convert**, or run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:
630	
631	```sh
632	defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport always
633	```
634	
635	With `always` set, `import_media` and `relink_media` convert without asking, and the import can take as long as the conversion does. `import_media` then gives the converted file as `path` and the file you named as `original`, as it does for a WebM copy. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
636

3	description: "Find, read and manage every file a project has imported, from the list on the inspector's Media tab."
4	---
5

7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	The **Media** tab is the project's library: every file you've imported, whether a clip uses it or not. Come here to find a file, see what it is, put it on the timeline, or sort out one that has gone missing.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where={['Inspector ▸ Media', 'Right-click a row for its menu']}
13	  tools={['get_project', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'set_selection', 'relink_media', 'remove_media']}
14	/>
15	
16	<Shot
17	  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
18	  alt="The Media tab with three files. At the top, an Add Media… button with its shortcut ⇧⌘I and the count 3 items. Below it a Search by name field, a Sort popup set to Import Order and an Unused only checkbox. The rows show speech.mov with a thumbnail and the line 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 f…, and toneA.m4a and toneB.m4a with a waveform glyph and their durations, all three with a green audio badge. A Consolidate… button sits under the list, followed by the Camera Log and Cursor sections."

20	
21	## What the tab shows
22	
23	A project points at your files where they are, and doesn't copy them in. That's why a row can be missing, and why the tab offers **Relink…** and **Consolidate…**.
24	
25	From top to bottom, the tab holds:
26	
27	- **The top bar:** **Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>) and [the item count](#the-item-count). See [Import media](/projects/import-media/). You can also drop files from the Finder onto the tab to add them.
28	- **The find band:** [a search field](#search-by-name), [a sort](#sort) and [Unused only](#unused-only). With no media yet, this band isn't there and the tab reads "Drop files here, or use Add Media…."
29	- **The list:** one row per file.
30	- **The footer:** **Consolidate…**, with the line "Copies sources into the package". See [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).
31	
32	Three more sections sit under the list and work on the [selected row](#select-a-row):
33	
34	| Section | Appears once the project has | See |
35	| --- | --- | --- |
36	| **Camera Log** | A video file | [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) |
37	| **HDR10** | An HDR10 (PQ) file | [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) |
38	| **Cursor** | A movie that has a picture, not only sound | [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) |
39	
40	## Read a row
41	
42	Each row has a thumbnail, the file's name, and a line of facts that depends on the kind of file.
43	
44	| Kind | Thumbnail | The line reads |
45	| --- | --- | --- |
46	| Movie | A frame from the movie | Duration, size and frame rate, such as `00:01:12:04 · 1920×1080 · 29.97 fps` |
47	| Picture | The picture | Width × height and `30 fps`, such as `3024×4032 · 30 fps` |
48	| Sound | A waveform glyph | Duration |
49	| LUT | A cube glyph | `LUT` |
50	
51	A file with no duration or size shows its kind instead. Thumbnails arrive a moment after an import, and until then a glyph stands in. A line too long for the row ends in an ellipsis, so widen the inspector to read the rest.
52	
53	### Badges
54	
55	Badges sit at the right of a row:
56	
57	- **audio**, in green, marks a file with sound.
58	- **missing**, in coral, marks a file Frame Job can't find. It's always shown, however little room the row has, because the name and the line give way first. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
59	
60	### The tooltip
61	
62	Hover over a row to see how to place it: "Drag to a timeline track, or onto the canvas. Hold ⌥ to insert, ⇧⌥ to overwrite."
63	
64	A LUT's tooltip reads "A LUT: apply it to clips as a look."
65	
66	A file Frame Job made a movie copy of, such as a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) or a [conversion with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), has one more line above that. It gives the original's path and where the copy lives: Frame Job's Rewrapped folder, or this project's package once you've [consolidated](/projects/consolidate-media/#webm-mkv-and-converted-files).
67	
68	## Find a file
69	
70	### Search by name
71	
72	Type in **Search by name** and the list narrows as you type. It ignores case and accents, as the Finder does, so "resume" finds "Résumé.mov". Every character you type counts, including a space. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to clear the field.
73	
74	If nothing matches, or nothing is left once [Unused only](#unused-only) is on too, the tab reads "No media matches the search or the filter."
75	
76	### Sort
77	
78	The **Sort** popup puts the list in one of four orders. The default is **Import Order**.
79	
80	| Sort | Order |
81	| --- | --- |
82	| **Import Order** | The order the files were added. |
83	| **Name** | Alphabetical, the way the Finder sorts, so `clip2` comes before `clip10`. |
84	| **Duration** | Shortest first. Pictures and LUTs have no duration, so they come first. |
85	| **Kind** | Audio, Image, LUT, then Video. |
86	
87	Every order is ascending, and files that tie stay in import order.
88	
89	### Unused only
90	
91	Tick **Unused only** to show only the files no clip uses. It's a quick way to see what you could [remove](/projects/remove-media/) before you hand a project on.
92	
93	- A file used only inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) counts as used.
94	- A LUT counts as used when it's a clip's look or a file's Camera Log. A LUT used only as the look at the end of an action counts as unused.
95	
96	### The item count
97	
98	The top bar counts the files, and how many are showing while the list is narrowed:
99	
100	| Count | Means |
101	| --- | --- |
102	| No media | The project has no files. |
103	| 1 item, 12 items | Every file is showing. |
104	| 3 of 12 items | A search or Unused only is hiding the rest. |
105	
106	The search, the sort and Unused only belong to the window. They aren't saved with the project, and each open project has its own. They do survive an import, so a search stays on while you add more files.
107	
108	## Select a row
109	
110	Click a row to select it. The row gets an outline in the accent colour, and it becomes the file these work on:
111	
112	- **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** and **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**, which stay off until a row other than a LUT is selected. See [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/).
113	- The Camera Log, HDR10 and Cursor sections under the list.
114	
115	Selecting a row isn't an edit. It adds no undo step and doesn't mark the project as changed. If a search or Unused only hides the selected row, the row is deselected, so you can't place a file you can't see.
116	
117	## The row's menu
118	
119	Right-click a row for its menu. It acts on the row you clicked, whatever the selected row is.
120	
121	| Item | What it does |
122	| --- | --- |
123	| **Insert at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead and makes room for it. Off for a LUT. |
124	| **Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead and takes the room it needs. Off for a LUT. |
125	| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects the clips showing this file. See [below](#reveal-in-timeline). |
126	| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder. See [below](#reveal-in-finder). |
127	| **Relink…** | Points this row at another file. See [Relink one file](/projects/relink-media/#relink-one-file). |
128	| **Remove** | Takes the file out of the project. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/). |
129	
130	**Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** also select the row. They use the same track as the **Edit** menu's items, the selected clip's track or else the front track, and [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/) has the rest. A LUT is never placed, because it's [applied as a look](/color/luts/). A LUT row doesn't drag either.
131	
132	### Reveal in Timeline
133	
134	**Reveal in Timeline** shows you where you used a file. It selects every clip showing the file and scrolls to the earliest one. If that changes the selection, the inspector switches to the Clip tab. For a LUT, it selects the clips whose look it is.
135	
136	The item is off when nothing in the timeline itself uses the file, and that includes a file whose only clips are inside a nest. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> first: the command looks at whatever's open, so it then finds the clips in there.
137	
138	Revealing clips changes the selection, not the project. It adds no undo step.
139	
140	### Reveal in Finder
141	
142	**Reveal in Finder** shows the file in the Finder. For a WebM, an MKV or another file Frame Job made a copy of, it shows the original, or the copy when the original has gone. With neither on disk, it beeps.

158	
159	Removing media takes a file off the project's list. It never touches the file on your disk, and one undo brings it back.

162	  where="Right-click a row on the Media tab ▸ Remove"

165	
166	## Remove a file
167	
168	Right-click the file's row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) and choose **Remove**.
169	
170	If no clip uses the file, it goes at once, with no question, as one undo step called **Remove Media**.
171	
172	To see what you can remove without losing a clip, tick [Unused only](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only) first.
173	
174	## Remove a file clips use
175	
176	If clips use the file, Frame Job asks first, because a clip can't stay in a project without its file. The alert reads "Remove “name”? It is used by 3 clips, which will be removed with it."
177	
178	- **Remove and Delete Clips** removes the file and those clips as one undo step.
179	- **Cancel** changes nothing.
180	
181	The count covers the whole project, including clips inside [nests](/editing/nests/), even while a nest is open. The clips go from wherever they are:
182	
183	- Clips on the timeline leave their time empty. The clips around them don't move.
184	- Clips inside a nest go from the nest. The nest itself stays, with everything else in it.
185	
186	If you'd rather keep the clips and use another file, [relink](/projects/relink-media/#relink-one-file) instead.
187	
188	## What stays on disk
189	
190	Remove never deletes a file:
191	
192	- Your original stays where it is.
193	- A copy in the project's package, from [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/), stays in the package's `media` folder.
194	- A movie copy Frame Job made of a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) stays in its Rewrapped folder.
195	
196	## Good to know
197	
198	- Removing a LUT works differently: its clips stay and lose their look, and the alert's button reads **Remove and Clear Looks**. See [Remove a LUT in use](/color/luts/#remove-a-lut-in-use).
199	- If a clip's [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) follows the file you remove, Hide While Silent turns off on that clip. The clip stays.
200	- You can remove a file with a nest open. It still comes out of the whole project.
201	
202	## With an agent
203	
204	`remove_media` doesn't ask. It won't remove a file that clips still use unless the call passes `with_clips: true`, which takes those clips too. Without it, the call stops and names the clips in the way. For a LUT, `with_clips` clears the looks and Camera Logs that name it and keeps the clips. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

214	title: "Relink missing media"
215	description: "Point a project back at files that have moved, one at a time or a whole folder at once, and see what a relink changes and keeps."
216	---
217	
218	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
219	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
220	
221	A project points at your files where they are, so moving or deleting one leaves its clips with nothing to show. Relinking tells Frame Job where the file is now, or gives it another file to use instead.
222	
223	<AtAGlance
224	  where={['The Missing media sheet, when a project opens', 'Right-click a row on the Media tab ▸ Relink…']}
225	  tools={['relink_media', 'get_project']}
226	/>
227	
228	## When a file goes missing
229	
230	A project always opens, even with files gone. For each missing file:
231	
232	- Its clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, with no sound.
233	- Its row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wears a coral **missing** badge.
234	- An export still runs, and writes the slate and silence for those clips.
235	
236	Frame Job remembers a file by more than its path, so one you've moved or renamed is often still found and never shows as missing.
237	
238	## Relink from the Missing media sheet
239	
240	When a project opens with files missing, the **Missing media** sheet comes up. It reads "The project opened without these files: their clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate until the files are found." Each file is listed with its old path, and the footnote counts them ("3 files").
241	
242	<Steps>
243	
244	1. Choose **Locate…** beside a file.
245	
246	2. Pick its new location in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”." Its path appears in the row, and the button turns into **Change…**.
247	
248	3. Check the other rows. Frame Job has [looked in the same folder](#locate-one-file-find-the-rest) for them.
249	
250	4. Choose **Relink**.
251	
252	</Steps>
253	
254	**Relink** stays off until at least one file is located, then applies every choice as one undo step called **Relink Media**. You don't have to locate them all. The ones you skip stay missing, and you can [relink them later](#relink-one-file). **Cancel** changes nothing.
255	
256	The sheet is offered once, when the project's window opens, and doesn't appear over another sheet. After that, use the Media tab.
257	
258	### Locate one file, find the rest
259	
260	Choosing a file also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files, by name. So a shoot moved as one folder is usually found with one **Locate…**.
261	
262	Only the folder you pointed at is searched. A row is filled only if a file of that name is there, and a row that already has a file keeps it.
263	
264	## Relink one file
265	
266	To relink at any time, right-click the file's row on the Media tab, choose **Relink…**, and pick the file in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”."
267	
268	This works for any file, missing or not, so you can use it to swap one file for another across every clip that shows it. It's one undo step, **Relink Media**. Thumbnails and waveforms are rebuilt if the new file is a different one, and a file that has only moved keeps them.
269	
270	## What Frame Job checks
271	
272	Frame Job reads the new file the way it reads an import:
273	
274	- **It must be the same kind of file.** You can't relink a movie to a sound file, for example. From the Media tab you get a beep and the reason at the foot of the inspector. In the sheet, the other relinks are applied first and then an alert gives the reason. The row stays as it was either way.
275	- **It must be readable.** A file Frame Job can't open brings up an alert, and the sheet's other choices still go through.
276	- **A WebM or MKV is copied as it is on import.** See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). Choosing **Cancel** during the copy leaves that file out of the relink. A file macOS can't open can go through the same [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) as an import.
277	
278	## What a relink changes
279	
280	The row takes on the new file's duration, size, frame rate, and whether it has audio, video and alpha.
281	
282	A clip that runs past the end of a shorter new file is shortened to end with it, on the timeline and inside [nests](/editing/nests/). A clip that starts past the new end is cut down to a single frame. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and everything else about the clip stays as it was.
283	
284	A different file is analysed again, so features that use the analysis, such as [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/), wait for the new answers.
285	
286	## What a relink keeps
287	
288	Some things don't come from the new file, so here's what happens to each:
289	
290	| What | After a relink |
291	| --- | --- |
292	| [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) | Kept. It's your reading of the footage, which a new path doesn't change. |
293	| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) | Kept. The peak is read only at import, so set it by hand if the new file differs. |
294	| [Cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | The one beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the existing one stays, as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file. |
295	| Saved speech, for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) | What still fits in the new file is kept. A new file with no sound forgets it. |
296	
297	## Good to know
298	
299	- A file in the Trash isn't missing yet. Frame Job follows it there and keeps playing it until you empty the Trash.
300	- A project opened from a consolidated package that has moved finds its own copies, with no sheet. See [Move a consolidated package](/projects/consolidate-media/#move-a-consolidated-package).
301	- If a WebM or MKV copy has gone but the original is still there, Frame Job makes the copy again when the project opens. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
302	- A relink stores what Frame Job needs to follow the file, so the next move is followed too.
303	- You can relink with a nest open. The change still applies to the whole project.
304	
305	## With an agent
306	
307	`get_project` lists the files that need relinking under `missing_media`, and `relink_media` points one at a new path, with the same checks. It makes the bookmark that follows the file for you, or takes one you pass. It works on one file at a time and doesn't search a folder. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
308

317	title: "Consolidate Media"
318	description: "Copy every file a project uses into its package, so you can hand it over, move it or archive it without the originals."
319	---
320	
321	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
322	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
323	
324	A project normally points at your files where they are. Consolidate Media copies them all into the `.framejob` package and points the project at the copies, so the package becomes the whole edit. You can then hand it to someone, move it, or archive it and delete the originals.
325	
326	<AtAGlance
327	  menu="File ▸ Consolidate Media…"
328	  where="Media tab footer ▸ Consolidate…"
329	  tools="consolidate_media"
330	  needs="A saved project, and room on the disk for a second copy of the footage."
331	/>
332	
333	## Consolidate a project
334	
335	<Steps>
336	
337	1. Choose **File ▸ Consolidate Media…**, or **Consolidate…** at the foot of the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). Both are off when the project has no media. If the project has never been saved, you'll [save it first](#save-the-project-first).
338	
339	2. Watch the **Consolidating Media** sheet as the files copy.
340	
341	3. Read what the sheet reports, then choose **Close**, or **Show in Finder** to see the copies.
342	
343	</Steps>
344	
345	Every file in the media list is copied into a `media` folder inside the package, whether a clip uses it or not. To keep the package smaller, [remove](/projects/remove-media/) what you don't need first. [Unused only](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only) shows you what that is.
346	
347	## Save the project first
348	
349	An untitled project has no package to copy into. On one, the command asks "Save this project first?" and offers **Save…** and **Cancel**. After the save it carries on where it left off. Cancelling the Save panel stops the command.
350	
351	## While it copies
352	
353	The sheet shows a bar, a line such as "Copying 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package…", and the name of the file being copied. When every file is already inside and only the project's links need correcting, the line reads "Relinking 2…".
354	
355	**Cancel** stops between files, so the sheet shows "Stopping…" until the file in progress is done. What was copied stays copied and the project points at it, and the rest keep pointing at the originals. The project always opens. Run the command again to copy the rest.
356	
357	## When it finishes
358	
359	The sheet says what happened and offers **Show in Finder** and **Close**. **Show in Finder** shows the package's `media` folder and closes the sheet. The changes to the project are one undo step called **Consolidate Media**.
360	
361	| The sheet says | What it means |
362	| --- | --- |
363	| "Copied 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package." | How many files it copied, cursor files included. |
364	| "No files needed copying." | Nothing was copied. It also appears beside the lines below when no copy succeeded. |
365	| "Stopped before the rest." | You chose **Cancel**. |
366	| "2 files could not be copied." | Those files keep pointing at their originals, so every clip still plays. The first file's reason shows underneath. |
367	| "1 missing file was left alone — relink intro.mov." | See [Missing files](#missing-files). It names up to three. |
368	| "1 cursor file was missing and left alone." | See [Cursor files](#cursor-files). |
369	
370	## What gets copied
371	
372	### Names and duplicates
373	
374	- Two different files with the same name are kept apart, as `intro.mov` and `intro-2.mov`. Names are compared without regard to case, and a name already in the `media` folder counts as taken.
375	- Two rows in the media list that point at the same file share a single copy.
376	- Files already in the package's `media` folder aren't copied again.
377	
378	### Missing files
379	
380	A missing file can't be copied, so it's left alone and the sheet names it. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/) and consolidate again.
381	
382	With nothing to do, Frame Job doesn't open the sheet. It shows an alert reading "Nothing to consolidate." and why:
383	
384	- "Every file this project uses is already inside the package."
385	- "Every file this project can find is already inside the package. 2 missing files need relinking first."
386	
387	### LUTs
388	
389	[LUTs](/color/luts/) are in the media list, so they're copied like footage, used or not. The looks and Camera Logs that use one then read the copy in the package.
390	
391	### Cursor files
392	
393	A screen recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) is copied too, next to its movie and named after it: `Recording.mov` and `Recording.fjcursor`. It counts as one of the files copied in the final report.
394	
395	- It's copied only once its movie is, and the project points at the copy only once it's there.
396	- One that can't be copied is listed with the other failures, and the recording keeps its original cursor file.
397	- One that's missing is left alone: "1 cursor file was missing and left alone."
398	
399	### WebM, MKV and converted files
400	
401	For a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/), or a file [converted with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), Frame Job copies the movie it plays from, not the file you imported. The row's [tooltip](/projects/media-tab/#the-tooltip) then says it was copied into this project's package.
402	
403	## Move a consolidated package
404	
405	Move or rename a consolidated package and it finds its own copies when it opens. Any missing file with a file of the same name in the package's `media` folder is pointed back at it, and a screen recording's cursor file is found again the same way.
406	
407	This happens with no sheet, adds no undo step, and doesn't mark the project as changed. A file Frame Job can still find is never touched, even if a file of the same name sits in `media`. Anything still missing after this brings up the [Missing media sheet](/projects/relink-media/#relink-from-the-missing-media-sheet).
408	
409	## Good to know
410	
411	- Nothing checks for free space first. A copy that runs out of room is reported with the files that couldn't be copied, and those files keep pointing at their originals.
412	- Undo points the project back at the originals but leaves the copies in the package. Consolidating again then makes second copies, such as `intro-2.mov`.
413	- When two rows share a copy and that copy fails, both keep pointing at the original.
414	
415	## With an agent
416	
417	`consolidate_media` does the same work with no sheet and no **Cancel**, and Frame Job's own window doesn't respond until the copy is done, which can take a while. On a project that has never been saved it stops and says to save first. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you before it runs it. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
418

427	title: "On-device media analysis"
428	description: "What Frame Job works out about your files on this Mac, when it runs, how to stop it, and where the results are kept."
429	---
430	
431	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
432	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
433	
434	Frame Job studies your files so its commands know where the cuts fall, who's in frame and when someone is talking. All of it happens on this Mac, with no upload, no network request and no key.
435	
436	<AtAGlance
437	  menu={['Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes', 'Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Background', 'Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
438	  where={['The Analyzing sheet', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background']}
439	  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'analyze_cutout', 'split_at_shots', 'reframe_clip', 'detect_silence', 'set_media_speech', 'set_video', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
440	  needs="Nothing. Every analysis runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
441	/>
442	
443	This page explains the analysis itself. How to use a result is on the page of the feature that uses it.
444	
445	## What Frame Job works out
446	
447	| Result | When it's made | What uses it |
448	| --- | --- | --- |
449	| [Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness](#whats-built-when-a-file-arrives) | When a file arrives | The timeline and the audio tools |
450	| [Voice detection](#voice-detection) | When a file arrives | Remove Silences, Enhance Voice, Duck by Speech and others |
451	| [Shots](#shots) | When something asks | Split at Shot Changes, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version |
452	| [Faces](#faces) | When something asks | Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Switch by Speaker, Show Subjects |
453	| [People and salient regions](#people-and-salient-regions) | When something asks | Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Show Subjects |
454	| [Person masks](#person-masks) | When a clip needs them | Remove Background, Text Behind Subject |
455	| [Foreground masks](#foreground-masks-on-pictures) | When a picture needs one | Remove Background, Text Behind Subject |
456	| [Sound events](#sound-events) | When an agent asks | Agents only |
457	
458	## Analysis happens on demand
459	
460	Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. Frame Job does that when something asks for it: Split at Shot Changes, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Switch by Speaker, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject or an agent.
461	
462	Only the part that's needed is read:
463	
464	- Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and an agent reframing a clip ask for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side.
465	- Split at Shot Changes reads the parts its clips play, and skips any stretch of the file between them that no clip uses.
466	- A part that's already been analysed isn't read again, so a second request over the same footage starts at once.
467	
468	If two analyses of one file run at different times, what they find is added together. Neither replaces the other.
469	
470	## The Analyzing sheet
471	
472	When a menu command needs an analysis that isn't in the project yet, the **Analyzing** sheet comes up while it's made. When everything is already there, the sheet doesn't appear and the command goes straight ahead.
473	
474	<Shot
475	  name="15f-analyzing-sheet.sheet"
476	  alt="The Analyzing sheet for Split at Shot Changes. A sentence explains that nothing changes until the analysis is found and that Stop leaves everything as it is. Below it, the file speech.mov has an empty progress bar and the word Waiting, and a Stop button sits at the bottom right."
477	/>
478	
479	The sheet has one row for each file that needs work, with its name, a bar and a status:
480	
481	| Status | What it means |
482	| --- | --- |
483	| Waiting | Frame Job hasn't read the file's first frame yet. |
484	| A percentage | The share of the work done so far. |
485	| Done | This file has finished. |
486	
487	For [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), a file can have a row for each thing being found, such as "speech.mov — Faces", "speech.mov — Shot changes" and "speech.mov — People and salient regions".
488	
489	These commands use the sheet:
490	
491	- **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**
492	- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**, after you press **Follow** in its own sheet
493	- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**, after you press **Make** in its own sheet
494	- **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**, before its own sheet, when it needs to find faces because it's working from one microphone
495	
496	When every row is done, the sheet closes by itself and the command carries on. Every editor action is off while the sheet is up.
497	
498	If the project changes while the sheet is up, which an agent can do, the command makes no edit. The inspector says so and asks you to choose the command again.
499	
500	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) doesn't use this sheet. It makes its masks while you go on working, and shows its progress in **Status** in the Clip tab's **Background** section.
501	
502	### Stop an analysis
503	
504	Choose **Stop**, or press <kbd>Esc</kbd>. The sheet closes, the command is cancelled and no edit is made. What was already saved stays in the project, so choosing the command again carries on from there.
505	
506	Minimising the window also stops the work. When you bring the window back, the sheet starts again on whatever hadn't finished.
507	
508	### When an analysis fails
509	
510	If an analysis can't finish, the command stops instead of editing with half an answer. Frame Job beeps, and the foot of the inspector names the file and the reason, for example: "The shots analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …"
511	
512	If a file is missing or can't be read, Split at Shot Changes and Switch by Speaker stop before the sheet opens, and Follow Subject says so in its own sheet. Make Vertical Version keeps a clip whose file is missing as it's placed and goes on with the rest. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
513	
514	## Analysis runs in the background
515	
516	You can keep working while an analysis runs, except while the Analyzing sheet is up.
517	
518	- Picture analysis runs at low priority, one job at a time across all your open projects.
519	- Sound analysis has its own queue, so one sound job can run beside one picture job.
520	- Frame Job saves what it has found every 30 seconds, and at the end of each stretch of the file it reads. If a job stops part-way, everything saved so far is kept and the next request continues from there.
521	- A job that nothing wants any more is dropped if it hasn't started, and cancelled if it has. Closing a project does this to its jobs.
522	
523	## What each analysis finds
524	
525	### Shots
526	
527	Frame Job finds the hard cuts in a video by comparing each frame's colours with the frames before it. This is plain arithmetic, with no machine learning.
528	
529	- A gradual dissolve isn't reported as a cut.
530	- A single flash frame isn't a cut.
531	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can show as one cut.
532	
533	[Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/) cuts your clips at these moments.
534	
535	### Faces
536	
537	Frame Job looks for faces ten times a second of the file's own time, using Apple's Vision framework. For each face it keeps its box, how far it's turned and tilted, and how open the mouth is.
538	
539	Faces are listed from left to right. They carry no identity, so Frame Job doesn't know that a face in one sample is the same person in the next, and it never puts names to faces.
540	
541	### People and salient regions
542	
543	At the same ten samples a second, Frame Job finds:
544	
545	- **People**, as a box around each person's head and shoulders.
546	- **Salient regions**, as boxes around the parts of the picture the eye goes to first. In a talking-head shot that's usually the speaker, and on a slide it's often the text.
547	
548	Each sample is judged on its own, so no person is followed from one moment to the next. See [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) for how Frame Job uses them, and [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) to see faces, people and salient regions over the preview.
549	
550	### Person masks
551	
552	A person mask is an outline of a person, made for every frame of the video that a clip plays. [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) and [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) draw with these masks, and they're made when a clip has one of those on.
553	
554	A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half strength. The masks are kept at the size Vision makes them, one for every frame, so a long clip's masks take up room in the package: about 62 MB for a minute of 1080p video.
555	
556	### Foreground masks on pictures
557	
558	On a still picture, Frame Job can mask the foreground subject, whether or not it's a person. Turn on Remove Background, then choose **Foreground** in the **Subject** row of the Clip tab's **Background** section. The row appears when every selected clip is a picture, and **Person** is the default.
559	
560	Either way a picture gets one mask, made from the picture as it's drawn, the right way up.
561	
562	### Sound events
563	
564	Frame Job can listen to a file's first sound track and score how likely six kinds of sound are: laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. It uses Apple's Sound Analysis, in overlapping windows 1.5 seconds long that start every 0.75 seconds. Each score runs from 0 to 1, and there's no score where a window runs past the end of the sound.
565	
566	Only an agent can ask for these, and no menu or pane uses them. Treat the scores as hints, never as a finding on their own.
567	
568	The file needs sound, and an audio file works. Frame Job won't read sound events for a clip that plays in reverse, because its sound runs backwards.
569	
570	## What's built when a file arrives
571	
572	After you open a project, import a file or relink one, Frame Job builds these in the background, and the timeline fills in as they finish:
573	
574	- **Filmstrip thumbnails** for every file with a picture, which its clips show on the timeline. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
575	- **The waveform**, at 100 peaks a second.
576	- **The loudness record**, in 10 ms steps, which Normalize, Enhance Voice and the loudness read-outs use.
577	- **Sound-matching features**, which [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) uses.
578	- **[Voice detection](#voice-detection)**.
579	
580	At most two files' sound is read at a time, so a big import doesn't hold up playback or a speed ramp's sound. Anything already built for an unchanged file is never built again. A file with no sound has no waveform, loudness or voice detection, and a `.cube` LUT file gets none of these.
581	
582	Until one of these is ready, the controls that need it wait or read "measuring…". A command that needs it says the file is still being analysed and asks you to try again in a moment.
583	
584	If a waveform or loudness pass fails, Frame Job tries again after 2 seconds and again after 10. After that it tries the next time you open the project.
585	
586	### Voice detection
587	
588	Frame Job scores every 32 ms of a file's sound for speech, using the Silero voice model bundled with the app. That's how later commands tell a voice from noise. These use it:
589	
590	- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/voice-or-level/), in its **Voice** mode
591	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/)
592	- The [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
593	- [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/)
594	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
595	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
596	- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
597	- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/) and [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)
598	- The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), to place where a word on this Mac's reading really starts and to find the pauses between paragraphs
599	
600	If the voice model can't be used, Remove Silences says so and judges quiet by level instead.
601	
602	## Results are kept per file
603	
604	Anything Frame Job finds is kept for the file, not for a clip, in the project's cache, a folder of things it can make again. Every clip of a file shares it, and a second request over the same part is ready at once. Picture analysis and sound events live in the `.framejob` package under `cache/analysis/`.
605	
606	A result counts only for the file it was made from, which Frame Job checks by the file's size, modification time and length. Relink to a different file, or change the file on disk, and it's analysed again. An unchanged file isn't.
607	
608	Picture analysis and sound events also record the macOS build they were made on. After a macOS update, or on a Mac running a different build, they're made again the next time something asks. The same goes when a Frame Job update changes what one of them stores.
609	
610	## Results travel with the project
611	
612	The caches live inside the `.framejob` package, so they go wherever it goes. Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps them. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/) for what's inside.
613	
614	A new project made from this one starts with them too, so nothing is analysed twice. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) and the **Make a copy** option of [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) carry these, for each file the new project keeps:
615	
616	- Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness
617	- Voice detection and sound-matching features
618	- On-device transcripts
619	- Everything on this page that's found in the picture or sound
620	- The reversed render of any clip that plays backwards
621	
622	Your media files are never copied. Neither is speed-ramp audio, or a voice-isolated or voice-effect render, and those are made again when they're needed. A cloud transcript stays behind unless its copy on AssemblyAI has already been deleted.
623	
624	## Good to know
625	
626	- **Show Subjects** never starts an analysis. Where nothing has been found it reads "Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it".
627	- A package with a missing or damaged cache still opens, and what's built when a file arrives is built again. Picture analysis is made again when something next asks, but a lost cloud transcript costs money to make again.
628	- Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches sit in a temporary folder. The first save copies them into the package.
629	
630	## With an agent
631	
632	An agent can read the results themselves with `get_media_analysis`, for a whole file or for the part one clip plays, and it's the only way to reach [sound events](#sound-events). It shows no sheet. It waits at most 60 seconds, then stops and says how much it covered. What it covered is kept, so asking again carries on. A long file is read in windows, because one reply has a size limit. Each reply says whether it came from the cache alone, and what the result was made with.
633	
634	`analyze_cutout` makes a clip's masks and says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
635

8	
9	The Document tab holds what belongs to the project as a whole rather than to one clip: its size, its frame rate, its background and its markers. The canvas you set here is the fixed frame every clip is composited into, and every export starts from its size.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Inspector ▸ Document" tools={['set_canvas', 'get_project']} />
12	
13	<Shot
14	  name="11-document-inspector.inspector"
15	  alt="The inspector's Document tab. The Document section reads Resolution 960 × 540, Frame rate 30 fps, Duration 00:00:05:07, Tracks 5, Background Black and Colour SDR — Rec. 709. Below it are the Canvas section with its Preset, Width, Height, Resize clips proportionally, Dynamic Range and Blending rows, and the Frame Rate section with Rate and Duration."
16	/>
17	
18	## Open the tab
19	
20	Click **Document** at the top of the inspector. Selecting a clip on the timeline moves the inspector to the **Clip** tab, so come back here when you've finished with the clip.
21	
22	## What's in the tab
23	
24	The tab has five sections, from top to bottom.
25	
26	| Section | What it's for |
27	| --- | --- |
28	| **Document** | A read-out of the project. See [below](#the-document-summary). |
29	| **Canvas** | [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/), then the project's [dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/) and [blending](/hdr/blending/). |
30	| **Frame Rate** | The [project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) and the timeline's length. |
31	| **Appearance** | The [background colour, timecode format and Fit new clips to canvas](/projects/background-and-timecode/). |
32	| **Markers** | Every [marker](/timeline/markers/) in the project, in time order. |
33	
34	## The Document summary
35	
36	The first section tells you what the project is before you change anything. Its rows are read-only and update as you work.
37	
38	| Row | What it shows |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| **Resolution** | The canvas size in pixels, such as `1920 × 1080`. |
41	| **Frame rate** | The project's real rate, such as `29.97 fps`, even when the **Rate** popup [can't list it](/projects/frame-rate/#rates-the-popup-doesnt-list). |
42	| **Duration** | The timeline's length, in the project's [timecode format](/projects/background-and-timecode/#choose-a-timecode-format). |
43	| **Tracks** | How many tracks the project has. |
44	| **Background** | `Black`, `White`, a `#RRGGBB` value or `Transparent`. A colour that's only partly opaque also shows its opacity as a percentage, such as `#336699 · 50%`. |
45	| **Colour** | `SDR — Rec. 709` or `HDR — Rec. 2100 HLG`. |
46	
47	## How changes behave
48	
49	You can undo any change you make here to the project. The exception is **Resize clips proportionally**, which is a preference on this Mac rather than part of the project, so undo doesn't touch it.
50	
51	The tab always shows the whole project. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open it keeps working, and it changes the project rather than the nest. A nest keeps the size it was made at, whatever you do to the canvas.
52	
53	## With an agent
54	
55	`set_canvas` changes the size, rate, background, timecode format, Fit new clips to canvas, dynamic range and blending in one call. It must name at least one of them, and anything it doesn't name keeps its value. It works on the whole project, so a call addressed to a nest fails, while a call made with a nest open through `set_scope` changes the project, as the tab does. `get_project` reads the settings back. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
56	
57	## Related

63	title: "Canvas size"
64	description: "Set the project's frame from a preset, a source file or typed numbers, and choose whether your clips scale along with it."
65	---
66	
67	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
68	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
69	
70	The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is composited into, and every export starts from its size. Change it when the whole video should be a different shape.
71	
72	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Canvas" tools="set_canvas" />
73	
74	A new project starts at 1920 × 1080. A project opened from a movie or a picture takes that file's size, and one opened from a sound file starts at 1920 × 1080.
75	
76	## Pick a preset
77	
78	<Steps>
79	
80	1. Open the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).
81	
82	2. Tick **Resize clips proportionally** if you want your layout to [follow the new size](#resize-your-clips-with-the-canvas).
83	
84	3. In the **Canvas** section, choose a size from **Preset**.
85	
86	</Steps>
87	
88	The list runs in this order:
89	
90	- **1080p · 1920 × 1080**
91	- **4K · 3840 × 2160**
92	- **720p · 1280 × 720**
93	- **Vertical · 1080 × 1920**
94	- **Square · 1080 × 1080**
95	- **1440p · 2560 × 1440**
96	- **Source Size**, which [matches a file](#match-a-source-file)
97	- **Custom**, which the popup shows when the size matches none of these. Choosing it beeps and changes nothing, so [type the size](#type-a-size) instead.
98	
99	Each change is one undo step.
100	
101	## Match a source file
102	
103	Choose **Source Size** in **Preset** to set the canvas to the size of the first media file that has a picture size. It beeps when no file in the project has one, as in a project of sound files only.
104	
105	A file with an odd width or height can't be used. Choosing it puts up the same alert as [typing an odd number](#type-a-size), and the size stays as it was.
106	
107	## Type a size
108	
109	Type into **Width** and **Height**, in pixels. **Preset** then reads **Custom**, unless the size happens to match a preset or the first media file that has a picture size.
110	
111	- Both numbers must be even. An odd number puts up an alert such as "canvas width must be even (h.264 encodes in macroblocks), not 1081", and the size stays as it was.
112	- The range is 16 to 16,384. A number outside it is pulled to the nearest limit.
113	- A number with a fraction is rounded to a whole pixel.
114	
115	A project opened from an odd-sized movie keeps that size. Once you change either field, though, both sides are checked. If one side is odd, fix that side first. If both are, choose a preset, because a field can only change one side at a time.
116	
117	## Resize your clips with the canvas
118	
119	**Resize clips proportionally** decides what happens to your clips at the next size change. It's off by default.
120	
121	| Setting | What a size change does |
122	| --- | --- |
123	| Off | Clips keep their scale and their distance in pixels from the centre of the canvas. |
124	| On | Every clip's position and scale change by the same ratio as the canvas, so the layout looks the same at the new size. |
125	
126	When the shape of the canvas changes too, a clip's horizontal position follows the width and its vertical position follows the height. Its scale follows the smaller of the two ratios, so a clip that fitted the old canvas still fits the new one.
127	
128	The checkbox is a preference on this Mac. It's remembered across launches and it isn't saved in the project, so ticking it is not an undo step. The size change it scales is.
129	
130	## Good to know
131	
132	- A resize scales each clip's own placement. An [action](/motion/actions/) that moves a clip keeps its old target, so check any animated moves afterwards.
133	- Clips inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) aren't touched. A nest keeps the size it was made at.
134	- To turn a landscape timeline into a tall or square one, with each clip reframed, use [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/).
135	- Captions can follow a new canvas too. See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/).
136	
137	## With an agent
138	
139	`set_canvas` takes the size and, on each call, whether to scale the clips, with `rescale_clips`. It doesn't read the checkbox, so leaving `rescale_clips` out means the clips aren't scaled. A size outside the range isn't pulled to the limit as a typed one is: the call fails and nothing changes. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).

158	## Choose a rate
159	
160	In the **Frame Rate** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/), choose a rate from **Rate**: **24**, **23.976**, **25**, **30**, **29.97**, **50**, **60** or **Match First Clip**.
161	
162	The change is one undo step. See [what it does to the timeline](#what-a-rate-change-does).
163	
164	## Match the first clip
165	
166	**Match First Clip** takes the rate of the earliest clip on the timeline whose file has video. It beeps if there isn't one.
167	
168	It sets the rate once, and later changes to the timeline don't move it. The popup then shows that rate, if it [lists it](#rates-the-popup-doesnt-list). A picture counts as having video here, and it reads as 30 fps.
169	
170	## Rates the popup doesn't list
171	
172	A project can run at a rate the popup doesn't have, because a file's rate is kept as it is when you open it.
173	
174	- A file at 24, 23.976, 25, 30, 29.97, 48, 50, 60 or 59.94 fps keeps that exact rate.
175	- Any other rate is kept to three decimals, so a 47.3 fps recording stays at 47.3 and doesn't become 48. Screen recordings often have odd rates.
176	
177	:::caution
178	At a rate it doesn't list, **Rate** shows **24**. The **Frame rate** row at the top of the Document tab shows the real rate, so trust that one.
179	:::
180	
181	Choosing a popup item changes the rate. **Match First Clip** brings the file's own rate back.
182	
183	## What a rate change does
184	
185	Changing the rate moves every clip start, clip length, action and marker onto the new frame grid, inside nests as well.
186	
187	- A clip's length is held to the media it has left, so a coarser grid can't push a clip past the end of its file.
188	- A clip always keeps at least one frame.
189	- An action stays inside its clip. A speed ramp's action is only snapped to the new grid.
190	- Where a clip starts reading its source doesn't change, and sound fades keep their lengths.
191	
192	If two markers land on the same frame at the new rate, only one stays: the one added first.
193	
194	Frame Job doesn't check the new positions for overlaps, and it won't stop a rate change because of one. Each edge moves by less than a frame, so an overlap can grow by a frame at most.
195	
196	## Read the timeline's length
197	
198	**Duration**, under **Rate**, is a read-only row showing the timeline's length in the project's [timecode format](/projects/background-and-timecode/#choose-a-timecode-format).
199	
200	## With an agent
201	
202	`set_canvas` takes `fps` as `[numerator, denominator]`: `[30, 1]`, `[30000, 1001]` for 29.97 or `[24000, 1001]` for 23.976. Any fraction works, so an agent can set a rate the popup doesn't list, such as 48 or 59.94 fps. A 0 in either place fails and the rate stays as it was. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
203

210	title: "Canvas background and timecode"
211	description: "Set the colour behind every layer, make the canvas transparent, choose how times are shown, and decide how new clips are sized."
212	---
213	
214	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
215	
216	The **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) sets three things for the whole project: the colour behind your clips, how times are written, and how big a new clip starts.
217	
218	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Appearance" tools={['set_canvas', 'add_clip']} />
219	
220	| Control | What it does | Default |
221	| --- | --- | --- |
222	| **Background** | The colour behind every layer. | Black, opaque |
223	| **Timecode** | How the project shows a time. | Frames |
224	| **Fit new clips to canvas** | Scales down a new clip that's bigger than the canvas. | On |
225	
226	A change to **Timecode** or **Fit new clips to canvas** is one undo step.
227	
228	## Set the background colour
229	
230	Click the **Background** swatch and pick a colour in the Colors panel. The colour sits behind every layer, so it shows wherever no clip covers the canvas.
231	
232	To put a colour on the timeline as a clip instead, see [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
233	
234	## Make the background transparent
235	
236	Lower the opacity in the Colors panel. The swatch shows a checkerboard behind the colour, and the **Background** row of the [Document summary](/projects/document-tab/#the-document-summary) reads `Transparent`, or the colour with its opacity.
237	
238	Most export formats can't carry transparency, so while the background isn't fully opaque, the section adds a note about the formats that can.
239	
240	| The note says | When |
241	| --- | --- |
242	| "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats." | Three or more formats keep it, so the note counts them. They're HEVC with Alpha (MOV), VP9 with Alpha (WebM), ProRes 4444 (MOV) and Animated PNG. |
243	| "Transparent — needs an alpha format." | Frame Job can't name the formats yet, which can happen on a project with nothing on the timeline. |
244	
245	See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).
246	
247	## Choose a timecode format
248	
249	**Timecode** sets how times are written everywhere the project shows one, including the toolbar, the ruler, the inspector, markers and the transcript.
250	
251	| Choice | Looks like |
252	| --- | --- |
253	| **Frames** | `HH:MM:SS:FF` |
254	| **Milliseconds** | `HH:MM:SS.mmm` |
255	
256	**Frames** doesn't drop frames, so at 29.97 fps the count runs slightly behind the clock over a long timeline.
257	
258	## Fit new clips to canvas
259	
260	This decides how big a new clip starts. It's on by default.
261	
262	| Setting | A clip bigger than the canvas | Any other clip |
263	| --- | --- | --- |
264	| On | Starts at Fit scale: scaled down until all of it shows. | Starts at 100 %, its native size. |
265	| Off | Starts at 100 %, so it runs past the edges of the canvas. | Starts at 100 %. |
266	
267	A clip counts as bigger when either its width or its height is larger than the canvas. Fit never scales a clip up, and changing the setting leaves clips already on the timeline as they are. To fit or fill one clip, see [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/).
268	
269	## Reset the section
270	
271	**Reset** on the **Appearance** header puts all three back to their defaults: opaque black, **Frames** and on. It's offered only while one of them differs, and it's one undo step.
272	
273	## With an agent
274	
275	`set_canvas` sets all three, and anything it doesn't name keeps its value.
276	
277	| Argument | What it takes |
278	| --- | --- |
279	| `background` | Four numbers from 0 to 1, `[r, g, b, a]`. Three numbers, or one outside the range, fails and nothing changes. |
280	| `timecode_frames` | `true` for **Frames**, `false` for **Milliseconds**. |
281	| `fit_new_clips` | `true` or `false`, as the checkbox. |
282	
283	`add_clip` follows **Fit new clips to canvas** as the app does. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
284
